judges.verdict: All 23 builds pass go test, go vet and gofmt, have a README row, and handle the core matching cases identically in my probes: weak comparison, lists, multiple header lines, *, handler-set weak tags, and POST/404 pass-through. What separates them is a HEAD response that writes no body. B and I tag ServeContent's HEAD with the hash of an empty body, which is a wrong strong validator. K, N and R do the same, but only when the handler sets no Content-Length. Everyone else safely omits the tag. After that, the deciding factors are whether a garbage list member hides a later valid tag (strict, net/http-style parsing vs lenient), whether Flush streams or is silently buffered, and how much extra machinery was added beyond the spec. P, A, S and D come out ahead because they are lenient, safe on HEAD, stream on Flush, and stay compact.
